title: Gradle fingerprints a named Groovy task action across incremental builds
summary: Editing A to B left the named action up to date on the parent method. The merged method reran both action forms, and the incremental doFirst output matched a fresh B build. Both unchanged controls skipped correctly.

change.description: Gradle tracks the implementation of the closure supplied to a named task action when checking whether the task is up to date.

notes: Both sides run on one verified Gradle 7.6 distribution. The registered named-action method is compiled from each exact pin. The setup replaces this one method in the released AbstractTask class. A build init script checks the executing class bytes on every invocation. Both strict pin policies accepted the restored historical grolifant dependency. The full-distribution build has a separate verification job.
Each deployment checks the JDK fingerprint, ordered artifact digests, caller classes and original class providers. The same compiled caller runs both sides in fresh JVMs.
